page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.8-16 is an ARM-based compute instance built on the Ampere Altra processor platform. It delivers 8 dedicated physical cores operating at a consistent 3.0 GHz clock speed, mapping directly to 8 vCPUs with a single thread per core. This single-threaded core topology eliminates hyperthreading resource contention, ensuring predictable instruction execution across multi-threaded computational workloads. The system is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

This instance configuration does not include local storage disks, requiring all persistent storage and root operating system filesystems to be hosted on network-attached block volumes. It features one complimentary public IPv4 address for external network routing. Acceleration hardware is absent, as the instance features zero dedicated GPUs. Utilizing the 64-bit ARM architecture, application runtimes and deployment dependencies must support native aarch64 instruction execution. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio places constraints on large in-memory working sets, prioritizing raw core throughput over extensive caching.

From an operational efficiency standpoint, the Ampere Altra design achieves high compute density per core, delivering stable multi-core processing at reduced energy and infrastructure overhead relative to conventional x86 platforms. The VM.Standard.A1.Flex.8-16 is suited for multi-threaded build systems, ARM continuous integration and continuous deployment pipelines, containerized microservices, web application hosting, and distributed compute nodes where dedicated single-thread core execution is beneficial.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.8-16 is an ARM64 virtual compute instance powered by Ampere Altra processors running at a fixed 3.0 GHz clock frequency. It features 8 dedicated physical cores mapping to 8 vCPUs with a single thread per core, avoiding performance variations associated with simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, providing 2.0 GB per core in a compute-oriented allocation. The instance contains no integrated local NVMe storage and relies on external block volumes for persistent disk storage, while discrete GPU acceleration is not present. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is included. By leveraging energy-efficient ARM hardware, it provides predictable compute throughput for parallel execution tasks. This instance is suited for ARM continuous integration and build pipelines, containerized web services, microservice architectures, and distributed batch processing tasks that benefit from dedicated core allocations without requiring massive memory footprints.
